core_obligations: Assume M/IM is zero, write I = (f_1, ..., f_r), and let i < r be the largest integer such that N = M/(f_1, ..., f_i)M is nonzero, noting that if no such i exists then M = 0 (proof lines 26107-26110).
Conclude that N is derived complete as a cokernel of a map between derived complete modules, quoting the Serre subcategory statement (proof lines 26110-26112).
Use the choice of i to conclude that f_{i+1} : N -> N is surjective (proof line 26113).
Conclude that lim(... -> N -> N -> N) is nonzero, contradicting the derived completeness of N (proof lines 26114-26118).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finitely generated ideal I of a ring A and a derived complete A-module M, and asserts that if M/IM = 0 then M = 0 (source lines 26099-26104). The proof is a reduction to a single element. Write I = (f_1, ..., f_r) and let i < r be the largest integer such that N = M/(f_1, ..., f_i)M is nonzero; if no such i exists then M = 0 and the proof is done (proof lines 26107-26110). Then N is derived complete, being a cokernel of a map between derived complete modules, quoting the statement that the derived complete modules form a Serre subcategory (proof lines 26110-26112). By the choice of i, the map f_{i+1} : N -> N is surjective, so the inverse limit of the constant system (... -> N -> N -> N) is nonzero, contradicting the derived completeness of N (proof lines 26113-26118). The non-routine content is the choice of the maximal index at which the partial quotient survives: it converts the vanishing of M/IM into the surjectivity of a single multiplication map, whose derived limit is then forced to be nonzero.
